stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy licensed for sterile compounding prepares two products on the same morning: a sterile infusion for an outpatient, and a sterile preparation for a patient admitted as an inpatient in the same hospital under its institutional licence. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both containers must be labelled as a sterile compounded preparation.
The outpatient container must also carry the pharmacist-contact telephone number.
The telephone must be staffed during regular hours of operation and at least 56 hours a week.
The inpatient preparation must also carry the telephone number, since the pharmacy does sterile compounding.
The pharmacist reachable on that number must have access to the patient's records.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21 sets two distinct duties. All drug preparations compounded by a board-licensed pharmacy must carry a label notifying users and practitioners that the drug is a sterile or non-sterile compounded preparation. Separately, pharmacies engaged in sterile or complex non-sterile compounding must provide a telephone number fostering communication between patients and a pharmacist employed by the pharmacy who has access to the patient's records, staffed during regular hours of operation every day and not less than 56 hours per week, affixed to the container alongside the compounded-preparation label. That telephone paragraph does not apply to an institutional pharmacy licensed under c. 112, s. 39I where the sterile preparation is to be administered to an inpatient within the same hospital.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the compounded-preparation label duty reaches all such preparations.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the outpatient container falls squarely within the telephone paragraph.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: staffed during regular hours every day and not less than 56 hours per week.
choice_analysis.D: The telephone paragraph is disapplied for an inpatient preparation within the same hospital.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the pharmacist reached must have access to the patient's records.

related_facts: The carve-out is tied to administration within the same hospital, not merely to inpatient status
explanation.mpje_trap: One exception is written into one of the two paragraphs. Reading it as an exception to both strips the required compounded-preparation label from the inpatient container.

reasoning_steps: Separate the compounded-preparation label duty from the telephone-number duty
Apply the institutional inpatient carve-out to the telephone duty only
Check the staffing standard attached to the telephone number
